name: browser-use
headline: LLMapper Skill: Concept Maps from Articles
short_description: A Claude Skill that transforms articles, PDFs, URLs, or pasted text into visual concept maps using a four-stage LLM pipeline with Mermaid diagram output.
author: jorgearango

sections.overview:
LLMapper Skill is a Claude Skill that converts articles and documents into structured visual knowledge graphs, answering what a subject is about and why it matters. It accepts file uploads (PDFs, text files), URLs, and pasted text as input sources. The skill processes content through four sequential stages: generating focusing questions for the user to choose from, summarizing key concepts and relationships, structuring data as an RDF knowledge graph, and rendering a Mermaid flowchart diagram inline as a Claude artifact. Researchers, students, and knowledge workers who need to quickly map and retain complex information from articles will find this skill especially useful.
Convert a research paper PDF into a navigable concept map
Summarize a long web article as a visual knowledge graph by pasting its URL
Extract and visualize key distinctions and contrasts from dense text
Generate multiple conceptual perspectives on a topic and choose the most relevant
sections.setup:
No install command available. Check the GitHub repository for manual installation instructions.
`git clone https://github.com/jorgearango/llmapper-skill`
sections.usage:
```
Create a concept map for [TOPIC] using the llmapper-skill. Include at least 10 key concepts and show the relationships between them. Format the output as a markdown table with columns for Concept, Description, and Related Concepts. Focus on [SPECIFIC ASPECT] of the topic.
```
Copy

```
Here's a concept map for 'Renewable Energy Technologies' focusing on solar power:

| Concept          | Description                                                                 | Related Concepts                     |
|-------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|
| Photovoltaic Cells | Convert sunlight directly into electricity using semiconducting materials. | Solar Panels, Silicon, Efficiency    |
| Solar Panels      | Arrays of photovoltaic cells designed for large-scale electricity generation. | Grid Integration, Rooftop Installations |
| Grid Integration  | Systems that connect solar power to the electrical grid.                  | Energy Storage, Smart Grids         |
| Energy Storage    | Technologies that store excess solar energy for later use.                 | Batteries, Flywheels, Hydrogen     |
| Efficiency        | The percentage of sunlight converted into usable electricity.              | Thin-Film, Monocrystalline, Bifacial |
| Thin-Film         | A type of photovoltaic cell made by depositing one or more thin layers.     | Cadmium Telluride, Amorphous Silicon |
| Monocrystalline   | Photovoltaic cells made from a single, continuous crystal structure.        | Efficiency, Cost                     |
| Bifacial          | Solar panels that can collect sunlight from both sides.                    | Efficiency, Installation Angles     |
| Rooftop Installations | Solar panels installed on residential or commercial buildings.             | Net Metering, Incentives            |
| Net Metering      | A billing mechanism that allows solar energy system owners to feed excess energy back into the grid. | Incentives, Policy                   |

This map shows the interconnected nature of solar power technologies and their supporting systems.
```
requirements: Claude Code or compatible AI agent
